channel.title: Natural Sciences Museum Science Café Events
channel.description: Science Café events from the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Science Café (Jan 21, 2027)
item.description: Grab a bite from the Daily Planet Café and join host Chris Smith for our monthly Science Café. Gather with other curious minds at this after-hours event for an informal presentation and conversation about current science topics with guest experts. The Daily Planet Café is open 5–8pm with a full menu during the Science Café. This month’s speaker will be announced soon! Please copy the URL below to share this page!

item.title: Museum Untold Tour (Dec 19, 2026)
item.description: Join us on a fast-paced and engaging tour of the NCMNS! Experience the Museum’s exhibits like an insider. You’ll hear untold stories only Museum staff know, and discover hidden details among the dioramas. The tour begins promptly at 2 PM and lasts approximately two hours. The tour ends in the Daily Planet Café where you can grab a beverage (included) and socialize with your guide and new best friends. Guests under 18 are not permitted on this tour. item.title: Science Trivia (Dec 3, 2026)
item.description: What’s cooler than absolute zero? The answer is Science Trivia night at NCMNS! Questions feature a mix of science facts, current news, pop culture and scientific discoveries. Held in the Daily Planet Cafe the first Thursday of each month, this is a great opportunity to mingle with friends, compete for prizes and bragging rights, and perhaps even learn something cool. The Museum closes at 5 PM; the Daily Planet Cafe will remain open. Please copy the URL below to share this page!

item.title: Whiteville Teen Science Cafe: Burning for Quail (Oct 8, 2026)
item.description: Join us for our next Teen Science Cafe, “Burning for Quail”, on Thursday, October 8 at 6PM. During this program, we will begin to answer the question, “What does wildlife management mean?” Using quail as an example, this presentation, led by Hackney Deans, will dive into what managing for this species entails, the strategies being used today, and how the successful management of one species can benefit the environment as a whole.
